title: Edge operator cheatsheet and retrospective (PRD draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight PRD draft and operator cheat-sheet for customer-managed network onboarding and the associated audit/approval flows. It was written after the last pilot with two early customers and captures: concise operator steps, a compact evidence format ("proof postcards"), gate timing SLAs, sampling rules for audit logs, and a short retrospective on problems we observed in the pilot.

Scope:
- Customer-managed VPC handover and initial connectivity (wire-up, routing, firewall rules).
- Approval gate UX for operators and customer admins.
- Compact audit payloads for low-bandwidth edges.
- Runbook for common failures and a retrospective list of product fixes.

Primary personas:
- Edge Operator (Redwood customer-facing operator or SRE) — executes onboarding steps, performs rollbacks, reviews proofs.
- Customer Network Admin — approves handover, provides evidence (CIDRs, BGP fingerprints), validates connectivity.
- Redwood Security Reviewer — samples proofs and audit logs, escalates anomalies.

Success metrics (provisional):
- Median time-to-complete handover: <= 45 minutes (goal).
- Fraction of handovers requiring manual escalation: < 10%.
- Audit evidence bundle size (median): < 20KB for low-bandwidth customers.
- Rate of post-handover connectivity incidents within 48h: < 5%.

Operator cheat-sheet (single page flow):
1) Pre-check (5–10m):
   - Confirm customer has provided: vpc-id, region, allowed CIDRs, peering/shared subnet details, and KMS key ARN if using customer-managed keys.
   - Verify account mapping in Redwood console: tenant id, operator-of-record, contact email.
   - Run quick scan: `net-check --cidr <cidr> --probe-ports 443,22` (internal script).

2) Collect proof postcard (compact evidence): (guideline)
   - Fields we capture: timestamp, operator-id, customer-admin-id, vpc-id, route-table-hash, gateway-arp-sample, config-diff-hash.
   - Canonical format: Base64 gzipped JSON with top-level metadata + 1-line human summary.
   - Minimum required evidence to gate approval: vpc-id + route-table-hash + connectivity-sample (TCP/443 open) + signed acknowledgement by customer-admin (email/SLACK link ok).

3) Submit for approval (fast-path):
   - Operator uploads postcard via console or CLI. The system runs an automated verifier: checks matching route hashes and executes a reachability probe from our probe cluster.
   - If verifier passes, auto-approve after 8 min (configurable). If verifier flags mismatch — escalate to manual review.

4) Approval gates and escalation timeline: 
   - Fast-path (auto): verifier green -> auto-approve within 8 minutes.
   - Delayed approve: verifier yellow (minor diff) -> requires operator sign-off, auto-fails after 24 hours -> escalates to Security Reviewer.
   - Hard-fail: verifier red (missing or conflicting evidence) -> immediate manual review and rollback option.

5) Post-handover validation (10–30m):
   - Run integration smoke tests: model request roundtrip, sample KV cache behavior, and telemetry forwarding.
   - Schedule 48h rolling monitoring: increased sampling of requests, keep caching disabled for first 2h in conservative mode.

Compact evidence format (proof postcards)
- Design goals: human readable headline, machine-verifiable payload, small size for low bandwidth, tamper-evident.
- Example postcard (concept):
  -- headline: "vpc: vpc-abc12 — route-hash: 0x9f3a — op: achen — 2025-06-18T15:11Z"
  -- payload: base64(gzip({"vpc":"vpc-abc12","routes_hash":"0x9f3a","probe_sample":"tcp/443:ok@34.12.1.5","op":"achen","cust_admin":"pnair@cust.co","sig":"GPG-or-KMS-sig"}))
- Storage: postcards stored in compact index in object-store and linked to full audit-log segments when available. Postcards are first-class evidence for fast-path approvals.

Audit log sampling strategy (practical rules):
- Full logs kept for 30 days for Dedicated/Enterprise customers (configurable).
- For low-bandwidth/private edges we implement two-tier sampling: 
  - 100% postcard retention (small metadata).
  - 5% full packet-level telemetry retention for the first 72h post-handover, then 0.5% ongoing unless anomaly triggers retention expansion.
- Sampling decisions are recorded in the audit log with a sampling-reason tag and sampling-uuid so Security Reviewers can reconstruct context.

Runbook: common failure modes & quick fixes
- Failure: route-hash mismatch after operator upload.
  - Quick fix: re-run `route-diff` tool, ask customer for last config push timestamp. If config drift within last 10m -> reject and request quiesce window.
- Failure: probe shows intermittent 443 failures from our probe cluster.
  - Quick fix: rotate probe region, re-run probes from multiple vantage points, then escalate if >50% fail.
- Failure: customer-admin cannot sign evidence (air-gapped).
  - Quick fix: accept manual signed PDF + operator-collected postcard (operator attests in console), but mark as "manual-evidence" and increase sampling rate for 72h.

Retrospective notes from pilots (observations and product fixes):
- Observation: Operators spent the most time aggregating evidence and copying logs into email threads.
  - Fix: add a single-click "collect-and-attach" action in console to produce postcard and populate approval request.
- Observation: Customers resisted large audit payload uploads on slow links.
  - Fix: postcards + incremental full-log fetch on-demand (pulls only needed segments).
- Observation: Escalation noise due to unhelpful verifier messages.
  - Fix: verifier to return concise actionable reasons (e.g., "route mismatch: missing 10.1.0.0/16") and suggested remediations.

UX details (console):
- Single view: left column shows checklist, middle column shows postcard preview and raw payload, right column shows automated verifier results and timeline.
- Action buttons: Collect postcard, Re-run verifier, Approve (fast-path), Request-more-evidence, Rollback, Add-note.
- Audit trail: all operator actions must be stamped with operator-id; changes to approval state create immutable events (event id, timestamp).

Security and compliance considerations:
- Postcards include hashes and signatures; full payloads encrypted-at-rest using customer KMS when requested.
- Retention SLAs and export path must be visible to customer before onboarding.
- Provide a downloadable audit package (postcards + sampled logs + verifier trace) for SOC inspections.

Open questions (for product/eng discussion):
- Do we standardize on GPG-based signatures or our KMS-based attestation as the canonical signature for customer-admins? Pros/cons from pilot: KMS easier for infra-savvy customers, GPG still common for air-gapped manual processes.
- What is the default auto-approve timeout? Pilot data suggests 8–12 minutes balances probe timing and operator patience.
- Sampling thresholds: should we make the 72h elevated sampling configurable per-customer or per-install?

Next steps / short backlog (prioritized):
1) Build quick console CTA: "Collect and attach postcard" (engineering spike, 2w).
2) Implement postcard index + object-store pointer (infra task, 1w).
3) Verifier improvements: return structured remediation hints (eng, 2w).
4) Policy UX: per-tenant sampling toggles + default 72h elevated-sampling (product + eng, 1w).
5) Draft a short customer-facing onboarding one-pager explaining proof postcards and what we need to sign off (solutions eng, 3d).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add sample CLI output for `net-check` and `route-diff` into Confluence page referenced above.
- Create test harness for simulated low-bandwidth postcard uploads (infra + QA).
- Interview two pilot operators for more details about manual evidence workflows.

Appendix: minimal postcard schema (human-readable sketch)
- line1: headline (string)
- line2: base64-payload (string)
- line3: short human summary (string)
- storage: object-store-key -> `postcards/{tenant}/{date}/{uuid}`

This doc is intentionally informal — meant to capture operational learnings and a small set of pragmatic product commitments. Feedback welcome, esp from SRE and Security reviewers.

-- achen (Avery Chen)
